newsitem.title: CHINA: China auctions tickets for Beijing-Kowloon train line.
newsitem.headline: China auctions tickets for Beijing-Kowloon train line.

text.p: China has auctioned 42 train tickets made of pure gold to mark the September 1 opening of a line that will eventually link Beijing and the Hong Kong district of Kowloon, Xinhua news agency said late on Friday.
The tickets, weighing six grams (0.2 oz) each, were auctioned for a total of 278,700 yuan ($33,600) on Friday, Xinhua said. Ticket number 001 fetched 51,000 yuan ($6,100).
Winning bidders are entitled to a one-way ride within a year.
Rail authorities issued the golden tickets to mark the September 1 inauguration of a train service between the Chinese capital and the southern city of Shenzhen bordering Hong Kong.
The service will extend to Hong Kong's Kowloon district when the British colony reverts to Chinese rule on July 1, 1997.
Ordinary tickets for the inaugural run have been sold out, with long queues at the Shenzhen railway station, Xinhua said.

The Beijing-Kowloon railway cost 40 billion yuan ($4.8 billion) to build, making it the largest rail investment in China. It runs for 2,356 km (1,464 miles) over 1,045 bridges and through 150 tunnels.

The State Development Bank will have granted loans totalling 9.85 billion yuan ($1.2 billion) to the project by the end of 1996, the Financial News said. Construction of the line was completed in November 1995.
